Jamal (Eng Mgr): Hey @people-ops — quick Q: I'm planning to promote an IC to L4 with an effective date of 2026-05-01. What exact paperwork do I need to submit for comp changes? How long until payroll reflects it and is backpay applied to the effective date?
Lina (People Ops): Thanks! Please submit the promo packet via the Promo form: https://redwood.company/docs/promo-form (link). Include manager justification, updated role bullets, 2-3 examples of impact, and the proposed new base + target on-target earnings if applicable. For comp changes we need manager signoff + calibration committee approval. Typical processing time is 10–20 business days after complete packet.
Maya (People Ops): Adding details: payroll cutoff matters — if the comp change is approved and entered in the system before payroll cutoff for the pay period that includes the effective date, payroll will issue backpay to the effective date. If approval enters after cutoff, backpay will be included in next payroll cycle. If you need an expedite, flag the packet with "salary-exception" and include why it's time-sensitive (e.g., market retention, offer match).
Jamal (Eng Mgr): Are there different rules for lateral market-level adjustments vs promotions? Also does an internal equity adjustment trigger any additional approvals?
Priya (Director, Eng): For lateral market adjustments we still require the same packet but we label it as "comp adjustment" instead of "promotion." Higher-value exceptions (above band midpoint or >15% bump) are routed to Comp Council for a second sign-off. Equity refreshes are handled separately — open a 1:1 with Total Rewards to discuss grant timing; compensation approval doesn't automatically change equity.
hr-bot: Ticket created: #C-8342 — Promo packet received, assigned to Lina. Next update expected in 7–10 business days unless expedited.
Cody (Recruiter): Quick follow-up — if we have an external offer in flight, and manager wants to match, do we still go through standard packet or is there a faster path?
Lina (People Ops): If it's time-sensitive for offer acceptance, include the offer details in the packet and request "expedite". We can often move approvals faster for offer-match scenarios but need clear justification and numbers. Also note: updating comp for someone already under offer may require coordination with the recruiter to update offer letters.
Jamal (Eng Mgr): Got it — I'll assemble the packet today and mark expedite with offer docs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Maya (People Ops): Ping us in thread once submitted and we'll triage. Include peer/skip-level feedback if available to speed calibration.
Jamal (Eng Mgr): Will do. Appreciate the help!
